newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says its army will resist U.S. attacks.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says its army will resist U.S. attacks.

text.p: Iraq said on Thursday it would defend itself against any U.S. military action and would continue its defiance of U.S. and allied no-fly zones over its territory.

"Iraq will continue defending its national airspace. Iraqis and the Iraqi armed forces will meet any aggression. This is a natural right approved by international norms and agreements," Information Minister Abd-al-Ghani Abd-al-Ghafur told reporters.

The minister said there was no backing down from a pledge Iraqi President Saddam Hussein made on September 3, when he ordered Iraqi anti-aircraft gunners and pilots to shoot down U.S. and allied planes violating his country's airspace.

U.S. and allied warplanes police two no-fly zones in Iraq and on Wednesday Iraqi forces fired a missile at allied aircraft in northern Iraq, prompting Washington to embark on large military preparations to punish Baghdad.
The U.S. fired 44 cruise missiles at air defence targets in southern Iraq last week in response to Baghdad's military intervention on the side of a Kurdish rebel faction in northern Iraq.
Ghafur vowed that Iraq would repair and rebuild targets damaged by U.S. strikes and mocked Washington's threats of military action if Baghdad did so.
